en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on Standing on the Heels 22.
The Second Training Rule on Standing on the Heels:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks sat with their hands on their hips in inhabited areas… [as before] … “The training is to be observed:
‘I shall not sit with my hands on my hips in an inhabited area.
One must not sit with one’s hands on one’s hips in an inhabited area.”
Whoever, out of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area with hands on hips, whether leaning to one side or both, commits an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who is lacking mindfulness, one who is unaware, or one who is ill.
For one who has entered upon the rains residence,
for one in times of distress, and for one who is insane.
the second training rule is concluded.
